title: Order Intake Standard — Changes of Flow, Usage Pattern and System Class in Home Oxygen Therapy
content:
# Changes of Flow, Usage Pattern and System Class — Home Oxygen Therapy

## Standard

1. A change of flow, usage pattern or system class of Home Oxygen Therapy is made only on a new written order where the class requires a new order for a change, never on the patient's request alone.
2. A change of system class keeps the same payment period and paid-month count.
3. A change of system class is made only after a system change request on this oxygen record is approved. The basis is the system record: the request type, its status and the oxygen record it is filed on.
4. The new class's portable add-on is billable only when its own mobility rule is met.
5. A prescribed flow above the class's highest continuous flow needs a class that delivers it.
6. No extra charge to the patient arises from a change of class.

## Judgement table

| Point | Rule |
|---|---|
| What a change rests on | a new written order, where the class requires one; never the patient's request alone |
| Payment period after a class change | the same period, with the same paid-month count |
| Approval | a system change request on this oxygen record, approved |
| Portable add-on of the new class | billable only when the new class's own mobility rule is met |
| Flow above the class's highest continuous flow | needs a class that delivers it |
| Charge to the patient for the change | none |

## Hypothetical case

A patient on a class delivering at most 5 LPM receives a new written order for 8 LPM. The prescribed flow is above the class's highest continuous flow and needs a class that delivers it; the class change is made once a system change request on the record is approved, the payment period and its paid-month count carry over unchanged, and no extra charge arises to the patient.
